message.reasoning:
We need to generate new test cases for isTypeAllowedInSection covering other scenarios: types not allowed, sections not AUTHORITY or ADDITIONAL (e.g., Section.QUESTION, Section.ANSWER?), also boundary conditions: unknown types, invalid types (Type.check throws IllegalArgumentException?), invalid sections (Section.check throws IllegalArgumentException?). Also test behavior when system property dnsjava.harden_unknown_additional is true (default) vs false. The method returns false for non-allowed types in AUTHORITY or ADDITIONAL unless property is false, then returns true (since !Boolean.parseBoolean(...)). Actually return !Boolean.parseBoolean(property). If property true, return false; if false, return true. So for unknown types in ADDITIONAL (e.g., Type.CNAME) it will go to default return false if property true. So we need to test that.

We need to avoid duplication with existing cases (they already cover allowed types in AUTHORITY). Need tests for:

- AUTHORITY section with disallowed type (e.g., Type.A, Type.MX) -> expect false (assuming property true).
- ADDITIONAL section with allowed types A and AAAA -> true.
- ADDITIONAL section with disallowed type (e.g., Type.NS) -> false (or true if property false).
- Section other than AUTHORITY or ADDITIONAL (e.g., Section.ANSWER) -> default return false (or true if property false).
- System property set to false: then any type in any section returns true (since !false = true). So test with disallowed type and property false.

- Invalid type: e.g., -1 or some high value not defined, Type.check should throw IllegalArgumentException. Need to test that exception is thrown.

- Invalid section: e.g., -1, expecting IllegalArgumentException.

We need to know Type and Section enums. Not provided, but we can assume constants: Type.SOA etc. Section.AUTHORITY, Section.ADDITIONAL, Section.ANSWER, Section.QUESTION. Use those names.

Test cases groups: maybe "Authority Section - Disallowed Types", "Additional Section - Allowed Types", "Additional Section - Disallowed Types", "Non-Authority/Additional Sections", "System Property Harden Unknown Additional Disabled", "Invalid Type Handling", "Invalid Section Handling".

We need to include input values as strings? In existing test case they used 'Type.SOA' etc. We'll follow same style.

Expected: true/false or exception. For exception, maybe "IllegalArgumentException". Provide description.

Also need to ensure we set system property before calling method. In test case description we can note that property is set accordingly. For JSON we just specify expected behavior; maybe include note in description.

Let's craft JSON array.
